# Live Updates: Iran and Oman edge toward temporary Strait of Hormuz reopening plan, but Tehran insists U.S. lift blockade

Updated on: August 26, 2026 / 4:49 AM EDT
/ CBS News

## What to know about the Iran war today:

## Iran says reopening the Strait of Hormuz depends on U.S. ending the war, despite progress in talks with Oman

Iran's deputy foreign minister insisted Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz would not reopen until the U.S. lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports and vessels, and the "termination of the war."

Kazem Gharibabadi told Iranian state broadcaster IRIB "the blockade is not the only quid pro quo for the Strait of Hormuz."

"Another issue is the termination of the war," he said. "The termination of the war in a permanent and sustainable manner on all fronts, including Lebanon."

Iran and Oman, the two countries with coastline in the waterway, said in a joint statement Tuesday that they were discussing a proposal for a temporary route that would allow ships to transit through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as a plan to remove sea mines.

President Trump has said repeatedly that all mines have been removed from the strait.

## Iranians line up for gas after U.S. announces new sanctions

Long lines formed at gas stations in Tehran Tuesday after the United States announced fresh sanctions aimed at pressuring Iran into submission.

#### **The News**

Treasury Launches Major Economic Campaign Against Iran, Dubbed ‘Economic D-Day’

The U.S. Department of the Treasury on Monday initiated [Operation Economic Outcast](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0613/), an expansive whole-of-government campaign aimed at isolating the Iranian regime economically, following direction from President Donald Trump. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described the effort as an “economic D-Day,” drawing a parallel to the World War II Allied invasion of Normandy. “We are launching an economic onslaught against Iran’s financial connections around the globe. Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” Bessent said.

The operation seeks to cut off revenue streams supporting the Iranian government and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Treasury expanded the scope of potential secondary sanctions to five key sectors of the Iranian economy: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping. # US drive for China decoupling to rely less on tariffs

Exclusion lists and other bars are gaining prominence in administration efforts to build secure national supply chains

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) last month further expanded its decision its Covered List of foreign-made technology barred from the US market.

The Trump administration’s drive to develop secure US-based supply chains in energy, tech, robotics and logistics is expanding. Bars on products and named firms are becoming more prominent as tariffs face political and legal resistance.

What next

Exposed suppliers face multi-point pressure, with the FCC set to at least one goods category, likely energy storage systems or subsea cable equipment, to the Covered List before the end of 2026. US efforts to inhibit China’s development of strong national supply chains, via export controls and investment curbs, have been more targeted but are also likely to extend, widening the net of affected US firms.

* For business, compliance burdens will rise as the federal government demands increased transparency around supply chains.
